predecessors.name: Turco-Egyptian Sudan
predecessors.text: Equatoria south of the Mahdist front: the three Equatoria states of South Sudan with Wadelai near Lake Albert (the Egyptian province also took in northern Uganda, Lake Albert and West Nile)

successors.name: Mahdist State
successors.text: Equatoria (the three Equatoria states of South Sudan and the Wadelai reach), taken by the Mahdist State in 1889 according to the Mahdist State dossier

ledger.x: 1885: Emin Pasha, cut off from Khartoum, withdraws to Wadelai.
1889: the Egyptian outpost ends and the Mahdists take the province.
1889: Equatoria ends as an Egyptian outpost; Emin's men stayed near Lake Albert until 1890, when Lugard took them to Kampala Hill, and Stanley and Emin reached Bagamoyo in 1890.

wars.name: Mahdist War (Equatoria front)
wars.outcome: Equatoria cut off from 1883, Emin and his garrisons isolated; a British expedition reached Emin in 1886-1889 and he left; the Egyptian outpost ended in 1889.

certainty.note: A string of garrisons around the Nile and Lake Albert; no frontier is described.
